name: Ardon
title: Son of Caleb (son of Hezron) from the tribe of Judah
summary: In the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles, Ardon appears as one of three sons that Caleb, son of Hezron, had with Azubah—the other two being Jesher and Shobab. This Caleb must be distinguished from the more famous Caleb, son of Jephunneh, who spied out Canaan; Caleb, son of Hezron, belongs to an earlier generation, only three generations removed from the patriarch Judah himself. Ardon appears exclusively in this genealogical context and is attributed no actions or further descendants in the biblical texts. His presence in the family tree nevertheless underscores Chronicles' desire to document all branches of the tribe of Judah—the tribe that through Hezron's son Ram carried forward the Davidic royal line and the messianic promise.
roles: Mentioned in the genealogy of Judah

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy of Judah
keyEvents.description: Ardon is mentioned as one of three sons that Caleb (son of Hezron) had with his wife Asuba. The three sons are Jesher, Shebub, and Ardon.

keyEvents.title: Caleb's lineage through Hezron
keyEvents.description: After Asuba died, Caleb took Ephrath as his wife, and she bore him Hur. Ardon thus belongs to the older branch of Caleb's descendants through Asuba, while Hur represents the younger branch through Ephrath.

keyEvents.title: Hezron's descendants in the tribe of Judah
keyEvents.description: Hezron was the father of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb. Through the line of Ram came Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, and David. Ardon belongs to the branch of Caleb, a side line in relation to the main Davidic line.

versions.summary: Ardon was a son of Caleb (son of Hezron) and his wife Azubah. He is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Judah. Ardon is a lesser-known biblical figure, but his place in the genealogy links him to the important Hezron-Caleb line within the tribe of Judah.
versions.title: Son of Caleb from the line of Hezron
versions.reason: [major] Ardon is known only from the genealogy in 1 Chronicles 2 and belongs to the generation after Hezron. Hezron was one of those who went down to Egypt with Jacob (Gen 46:12). Ardon likely lived during the Egyptian period, not the conquest era. The epoch should be 'patriarchs' or possibly 'exodus'. 'Conquest' is most probably too late for Ardon, even though he may be confused with the more well-known Caleb (son of Jephunneh). Caleb son of Hezron is a different person from Caleb son of Jephunneh who participated in the conquest. 'Patriarchs' is the most fitting label.; [minor] The role 'patriarch' is somewhat misleading for such a little-mentioned figure. Ardon appears only in a genealogy without any described function. A more neutral role like 'ancestor' or 'descendant of Judah' would be more precise. Alternatively, 'member of the tribe of Judah' could be used.; [minor] The summary is acceptable but should clarify that Caleb son of Hezron is not the same person as the better-known Caleb son of Jephunneh to avoid confusion.; [minor] The description of the second key event states "Ardon's father Caleb's lineage" and includes verses 19–20, which concern Caleb after Asubah's death (when he took Ephrath as wife and had Hur). Verses 19–20 do not mention Ardon directly, but this is acceptable as context for Caleb's further lineage.; [minor] The description says "including Ardon's grandfather," but Hezron is indeed Ardon's grandfather – this is correct. The event is acceptable as context, but the broad verse range (vv. 9–18) makes it a very general event for a profile mentioned directly only in verse 18.; [minor] The event "Genealogy of the tribe of Judah" with verses 1–5 provides very general context and concerns Judah's sons, not Ardon directly. Consider whether this event is necessary.; [minor] Footnotes are missing. It would be helpful to include a note explaining the difference between Caleb son of Hezron and Caleb son of Jephunneh, as well as a linguistic note on the meaning of the name Ardon.

versions.summary:
Ardon was a son of Caleb (son of Hezron) and his wife Azubah.  
He is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as part of the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.  
It is important to note that this Caleb (son of Hezron) is not the same as the more well-known Caleb son of Jephunneh, who took part in the conquest of Canaan.  
Ardon is a less known biblical figure, but his place in the genealogy connects him to the important Hezron-Caleb line within the tribe of Judah, the tribe to which the Davidic royal house and the promise of the Messiah belonged.
versions.title: Son of Caleb (son of Hezron) from the tribe of Judah
versions.reason: [minor] The summary closely resembles version 1 in the introduction ('Arnon was a son of Caleb (son of Hezron) and his wife Azubah'). It should be rephrased to avoid repetition from earlier versions.; [major] 1 Chr 2:18 mentions Caleb and Azubah, but Ardon is explicitly named for the first time in verse 18 along with his siblings. Some textual traditions place the sons' names in verse 18, while others include verse 19. The reference is acceptable but should be verified. The main issue is that in some translations, verse 18 only states that Caleb had children by Azubah/Jeriel, and the sons (Jezreel, Shobab, Ardon) are also mentioned in verse 18. The reference is correct.; [minor] The era 'patriarchs' typically covers the period of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Caleb son of Hezron belongs to the generations between Jacob/Judah and the Exodus. 'Patriarchs' can be defended since the line of Hezron connects to the patriarchal period, but one could also argue for 'Exodus' or even an earlier epoch. It is retained as 'patriarchs' since it is closest.; [minor] The role 'ancestor in the tribe of Judah' is somewhat imprecise since Ardon has no known descendants in the Bible. A more accurate role would be 'member of the tribe of Judah' or 'mentioned in the genealogy of Judah'.; [minor] The footnote stating that Caleb son of Hezron belongs to 'an earlier generation' is chronologically problematic. Hezron was a grandson of Judah, while Caleb son of Jephunneh lived during the Exodus—many generations later. The wording is correct in direction, but it is important to emphasize that there are many generations between them, not just one.

versions.summary: Ardon belongs to the genealogy of the tribe of Judah and is mentioned in 1 Chronicles as one of three sons that Caleb, son of Hezron, had with his wife Azubah. The other two sons were Jesher and Shobab. This Caleb is not the same as the well-known Caleb son of Jephunneh who spied out Canaan – Caleb son of Hezron belongs to a much earlier generation, only three generations after the patriarch Judah. Ardon is mentioned nowhere beyond this genealogy, and his lineage is not carried forward in biblical sources. Nevertheless, his place in the family tree testifies to the significance of the Hezron-Caleb branch within the tribe of Judah – the tribe that carried forward the Davidic royal line and the messianic promise.
versions.title: Son of Caleb (son of Hezron) from the tribe of Judah
versions.reason: [major] Ardon belongs to the early genealogical history of the tribe of Judah (three generations after Judah), but its placement in the genealogy points toward the period before and during the sojourn in Egypt, thus leaning more toward the patriarchal era and extending into the Exodus period. Nevertheless, 'patriarchs' is defensible given that the Hesron-Kaleb generation is traditionally regarded as very early. Upon closer consideration: Hesron is mentioned among those who went down to Egypt (Gen 46:12), and Kaleb son of Hesron likely lived during the stay in Egypt, that is, at the transition between the patriarchs and the Exodus. 'patriarchs' is acceptable but not ideal – yet no better era exists within the available options. Retain 'patriarchs'.; [minor] Verse 20 concerns Uri son of Hur and his son Bezalel, not directly about Ephrat giving birth to Hur. Only verse 19 covers that Kaleb took Ephrat and she bore Hur. Verse 20 may be included for context, but strictly speaking, it is verse 19 that is most relevant.; [minor] The summary is well written and informative, but its opening structure resembles the two previous versions. A third version should be formulated more distinctly to avoid repetition. A rephrasing beginning from a different perspective is recommended.; [minor] Footnote 2 (theological) regarding the difference between the two Calebs overlaps thematically with information already present in the summary. It remains valuable as its own footnote nonetheless. No change is necessary, though it could just as well have been classified as 'historical' rather than 'theological'.

footnotes.text: The name Ardon (Hebrew: אַרְדּוֹן) may possibly be derived from the Hebrew root 'ard' (ארד), which can mean 'to go down' or 'to flee'. Some scholars have also suggested a connection with the Akkadian word ardu ('servant'). The exact etymology of the name remains uncertain.

Caleb son of Hezron (1 Chron 2:18) must not be confused with the much better-known Caleb son of Jephunneh (Num 13:6; Josh 14:6), who was one of the twelve spies and received Hebron as his inheritance. Caleb son of Hezron lived many generations earlier and belongs to the early links in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.

Hezron was the son of Perez and grandson of Judah (Gen 46:12). Through Hezron's son Ram runs the lineage that leads to David (1 Chron 2:9–16; Ruth 4:18–22) and further to Jesus the Messiah (Matt 1:3–6). Ardon belongs to a side line through Caleb that is not carried forward in the biblical genealogies.

The genealogies in 1 Chronicles were likely compiled after the Babylonian exile and served an important function in restoring and preserving tribal identity and land rights. Even lesser-known names like Ardon were included to ensure a complete overview of the branches of the tribe of Judah.

In rabbinic tradition, names in genealogies have often been interpreted symbolically. Midrash literature sometimes links seemingly unknown names to more well-known biblical figures by suggesting they are alternative names or nicknames.

1 Chron 2:18 presents a textual critical challenge: the Hebrew base text can be read as saying that Caleb took Azubah and Jerioth, or that Azubah had the nickname Jerioth. The Septuagint and other ancient translations render the verse differently, and it is debated whether Jerioth was another wife, a daughter, or a nickname for Azubah.
